nodes.label: RBAC design — locked decisions
nodes.rationale: User to Role to Permissions, many-to-many via role_permission. Permissions are fixed and developer-defined at build time and an admin never creates one; roles are created and edited by an admin at runtime; one role per user with no per-user overrides — if one person needs a different set, duplicate the closest role and adjust it.

nodes.label: PERMISSION_DEFS as the single source
nodes.rationale: PERMISSIONS, PermissionKey and PERMISSION_IMPLIES are all derived from it, so a new module or action is added there and nowhere else. A module may contain one level of submodules and no deeper, because the flattening stops being unambiguous. Every module and submodule must define a view action, enforced by the types, because module:view is what each route's load function checks — a module without one is unreachable by anybody.

nodes.label: Keys are built forward, never split back apart
nodes.rationale: A submodule action flattens action first, submodule second: admin + users + manage becomes admin:manage_users. Recovering the parts is impossible because _ is both the separator and a legal character inside a submodule name — admin:view_org_units reads equally well two ways and nothing in the string resolves it. So look a key's submodule up in PERMISSIONS, where it was recorded at build time while the parts were still separate; the permission table has a module column holding the parent only and no submodule column.

nodes.label: Every access check tests a permission key, never a role name
nodes.rationale: can("admin:manage_fuel"), never roleName === "Admin". Role names are runtime data an admin can rename, while keys are defined in source and cannot change underneath the code. Applies in route load functions, the hooks.server.ts guard, and show/hide conditionals in components, all through the helpers in src/lib/rbac/access.ts.

nodes.label: expandPermissions and implied keys
nodes.rationale: Holding a key means holding the keys above it in the nesting. PERMISSION_IMPLIES stores single steps only and must never be read directly; expandPermissions walks the chain all the way up and is idempotent, so it is safe to apply anywhere. Keys it does not recognise pass through untouched rather than being dropped, so a leftover database row never silently removes access it was already granting.

nodes.label: Admin roles and staff roles are never mixed
nodes.rationale: A user holding admin:view is sent to /admin and sees only admin pages, so a staff permission is unusable to them — typing /fuel is blocked by the ordinary guard, needing nothing special. The role editor therefore asks which kind up front and shows only that key set. Admin data pages mirror staff ones as separate routes rather than one route branching on permissions, because the admin table has features the staff table does not and keeping them together would tangle two interfaces.

nodes.label: Role editor auto-tick rules
nodes.rationale: Ticking any non-view action ticks that module's view, because managing a page you cannot open is meaningless, and unticking a view unticks every other action in that module. Save exactly what was ticked, since the ticked set already includes every implied key — but still run expandPermissions server-side, because someone can POST a role save by hand and the database must never reach a state the UI would not have produced.

nodes.label: The Roles page is super-admin only
nodes.rationale: Both Roles keys are absent from the role editor rather than greyed out, so no admin can grant them through the UI; they reach the super-admin role only via create-admin.ts and the sync backfill. admin:view_roles is withheld alongside manage because a Roles page nobody can edit has no reason to exist, so its read-only rendering is never built. This is the one admin page that does not follow the usual view/manage split.

nodes.label: The super-admin role is frozen
nodes.rationale: Only its description is editable; name, status and permission set are locked, and deletion, deactivation and duplication into a second role holding the restricted key are blocked. There is no is_protected column — protection comes from a live condition read from role_permission, namely whether the role holds admin:manage_roles, and exactly one role may hold it. Opening it shows plain text or badges rather than tickable checkboxes, which is why new admin keys can only arrive by script backfill.

nodes.label: Never zero holders, warn at two to one
nodes.rationale: Any delete, deactivate or role reassignment that would drop the number of active users holding admin:manage_roles to zero is blocked; taking it from two to one warns but is allowed. This is what makes a super-admin handover by creating a second account workable, with the two overlapping as long as the handover takes.

nodes.label: No user changes their own role; only a super-admin assigns super-admin
nodes.rationale: Prevents self-promotion and also self-lockout, where an admin strips their own admin:manage_users and loses access to the only page that could undo it. Together with the rule that assigning or unassigning super-admin requires holding admin:manage_roles, the grant path closes completely: a user manager can neither promote themselves nor a colleague, nor unilaterally demote one of two super-admins, since rule 3 only prevents the count reaching zero.

nodes.label: Role templates
nodes.rationale: Pre-checked defaults shown when an admin creates a role and nothing more; never saved as records of their own, and no connection survives once a role is created. The Admin template is derived by filtering every admin key except the two Roles keys rather than being listed by hand, so a new admin page is picked up automatically while the Roles page stays excluded.

nodes.label: create-admin.ts bootstrap (RBAC side)
nodes.rationale: Runs on the production server after build via tsx, reading source directly rather than build output. Finds the super-admin role by the permission it holds, never by name; creates it from the Super Admin template if none exists, otherwise reuses it and just creates the user. Server access is the real security boundary and the database-password prompt is a secondary check.

nodes.label: sync-permissions.ts
nodes.rationale: Permission rows are data, not schema, so drizzle-kit generate produces nothing for a new key and this script must be run after any PERMISSION_DEFS change. Four steps: upsert every key, report orphans without deleting them, backfill the frozen super-admin role with any missing admin key, and re-normalize every role to its implied keys. Orphans are only reported because role_permission restricts on delete, so clearing one means removing live role grants first — a deliberate decision, not one a script should make unattended.

nodes.label: Staff module actions beyond view (open)
nodes.rationale: Fuel is the only module with an approval step, so it is the only one that will need an approve key — controlling who may mark a physically signed slip as approved — and will likely need submit and possibly view_all. Electricity, water, paper, ESWM and GHG record data without approval. The exact key list is not decided yet.
